title: 2021 Fall AMC 12A Problem 13
statement: The angle bisector of the acute angle formed at the origin by the graphs of the lines \(y = x\) and \(y = 3x\) has equation \(y = kx.\) What is \(k?\)

solutions.text:
The bisector points along the sum of the unit vectors of the two lines: \(\dfrac{(1,1)}{\sqrt2} + \dfrac{(1,3)}{\sqrt{10}}.\) Its slope is \[ k = \frac{\tfrac{1}{\sqrt2} + \tfrac{3}{\sqrt{10}}}{\tfrac{1}{\sqrt2} + \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{10}}} = \frac{\sqrt5 + 3}{\sqrt5 + 1}. \]

Multiplying numerator and denominator by \(\sqrt5 - 1\) gives \(\dfrac{(\sqrt5 + 3)(\sqrt5 - 1)}{4}\) \(= \dfrac{2 + 2\sqrt5}{4}\) \(= \dfrac{1 + \sqrt5}{2}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: A bisector direction is the sum of unit vectors along the two lines: \(\dfrac{(1,1)}{\sqrt2} + \dfrac{(1,3)}{\sqrt{10}}\)
\(k\) is the ratio (second component)/(first component); rationalize the result
